exposure: Group RD1: Intrathecal ropivacaine (12 mg) + dexmedetomidine 5 μg
Group RD3: Intrathecal ropivacaine (12 mg) + dexmedetomidine 10 μg
Group RD2: Intrathecal ropivacaine (12 mg) + dexmedetomidine 7.5 μg
Group R: Intrathecal ropivacaine (12 mg) alone
outcome: Duration of sensory and motor block
Onset time of sensory and motor block
Incidence of adverse effects (hypotension, bradycardia, nausea, vomiting, hypoxemia, pruritus)
Postnatal Apgar scores (1 min, 5 min after birth)
Postoperative concentrations of β-endorphin (β-EP), cortisol (Cor), and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α)
cohort: 120 American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) Class I and II parturients undergoing elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia
finding: Intrathecal dexmedetomidine 5 μg as an adjuvant to ropivacaine prolonged the duration of sensory and motor block, reduced the incidence of chills, reduced intraoperative stress reactions, and did not increase adverse effects or the amount of intraoperative vasoconstrictor used in women undergoing cesarean section.
